about: How this project tuned each function: what was tried, what happened, what was kept or rejected, and what has not been tried. Every entry cites the document it comes from; numbers are quoted as the sources state them. Dates are the journal's own where it gives one; where the text gives none (entries 1-21, the development sweeps), the date is the day the commit that recorded the work was made.

functions.extraction: Extraction: models reading symbols and tags
functions.line_tracing: Line tracing and connectivity (tracer, parent rule, flow direction, sheet stitching)
functions.scoring: Scoring: the scorer and its controls
functions.generated_pids: Generated P&IDs drawn from a model (loops, stations, style)
functions.te_model: Tennessee Eastman model: source and topology verification, tag conventions
functions.replay_and_bands: Replay, normal bands and fault detection
functions.ignition: Ignition and PI outputs: build, verifier, acceptance, screens

functions.review_loop: Review loop: operations corrections, mapping, outside review

(1) A 4-arm crossing counts as marked connected only if the residual ink also fills all four corners between its arms (at least the thinner run's width in pixels per corner, within the dot radius): a dot is a filled disc wider than the lines; stray pixels at a crossing (anti-aliasing, a thin line's ragged edge) touch both runs but fill only some corners, and strokes that touch only the two runs at an unmarked crossing are its own ink and join nothing. (2) A slanted residual stroke that carries on straight across a run (ink on both sides where it touches, each side reaching at least an arm's length, ARM_FRAC of a symbol side, from the run, the two sides on one straight line) does not join that run in the pipe layer: a label's leader drawn across a pipe to the next line, a dashed outline or hatching crossing a pipe. The traced output lists those points as slanted_crossings. Error classes found on development: OPEN100 sheet 1 (leaders across pipes, 5 crossing points), DEXPI C01 (26 'marked' crossings, 3 of them false junctions on the pipe; no development sheet had a real dot); the stray-pixel class was first seen on holdout sheet 6's images (allowed by A162 for naming classes), then confirmed on C01. Of the development errors left, OPEN100 sheet 5's (33 of 33 missed segments) come from line networks the tracer itself got wrong, and most others are key-graph omissions (an instrument leader or an arrow-tipped line drawn onto a pipe but not joined to it in the key), neither of which this layer can fix

(a) mode: BattLeDIM picks pressure n726 (median held-out R2 0.49, more than time of day's 0.20) and passes 1/14; MetroPT's mode tags (TP2, H1, Motor_current) explain little of the other tags (median R2 0.01-0.15) and nothing is chosen; forced Motor_current x time of day (b, R2 0.36) MetroPT 0/4. (c) time of day: 12 slots R2 under the threshold (not chosen); 24 slots 7/14; 48 or 96 slots 8/14. (d) without the median: 24 slots 5/14 (with 7/14). (e) fast 20: 9/14 (24, 48 or 96 slots); fast 6: 6/14; baseline 288 or 1200: 7/14, unchanged. (f) drift + median on every source: UCI 0/3 -> 2/3, MetroPT 1/4 -> 1/4 (failure 1 lost, failure 4 gained), BattLeDIM 0/14; PRONTO, SKAB, HAI and TE pass counts unchanged, but every detection 1 sample later (TE fault 6 18 -> 21 min, SKAB other/8 1 -> 421 s). attempts.runs: about 20 settings x 21 cyclic development runs; 2 full development passes (100 runs)
attempts.why: A mode found in a process tag can be moved by the fault itself (a leak shifts the zone pressure across the mode threshold, so the residual absorbs it: BattLeDIM 1/14); the clock cannot, so the phase kept is time of day. 48 slots kept over 24 (8 against 7 of 14); fast 20 (9/14) not kept: one run on one source, and it would be the only constant that differs from the drift method's. The median of 3 is kept inside the cyclic method (5 -> 7 of 14 at 24 slots) but not added to the drift default: it costs a sample of delay on every source for UCI's gain, which is a choice for the author, not a tuning step. Frozen as A184 before any held-out run (csv_normal_bands.py sha256 7713eceed011853f4e73764a577f90fd2202aac3d5e0d9408a367f7a76cd1463)

attempts.change: Frozen on the A178 development runs (sha256 recorded in A183), then BattLeDIM 2019 scored once: csv_normal_bands.py --method cyclic, and a new default --method auto that runs it when the data is cyclic by the clock. cyclic: each value minus its tag's time-of-day profile (the fit rows' mean in each of 48 slots of 30 min; a slot with under 3 fit values uses the tag's mean), a median of 3 samples (a single-sample spike never reaches the averages), then the drift method's 10-vs-600-sample gap on that residual; band = gap fit mean +/- max(K x gap fit sd, 1% of the tag's fit mean), not scaled with the reading; K = smallest of 10, 12, 15, 20 with under 0.5% of held-out normal rows flagged. auto: cyclic when the first column is a timestamp, the fit rows span at least 2 days and the profile fitted on them explains at least 0.1 of the held-out rows' variation (median tag, each tag's level allowed to move); otherwise drift, unchanged. The threshold 0.1 sits between the two development sources long enough to test (MetroPT-3 -0.003, BattLeDIM 2018 0.20)
attempts.hypothesis: A daily profile taken from normal running removes the demand cycle that sets the drift band's width, so a leak's step shows, and the choice can be made from the data
attempts.evidence: DEVELOPMENT, drift (A171) -> auto: BattLeDIM 2018 0/14 -> 8/14 (auto picks cyclic, R2 0.20; detected 9, one run over 0.5% pre-fault: p810 5/576 rows; the 5 abrupt leaks p673, p538, p866, p183, p158 at 25 min to 2.5 days, incipient p257, p31, p654 at 1.6-3.3 days); UCI 0/3 -> 0/3 and MetroPT-3 1/4 -> 1/4 (auto keeps drift: UCI has no timestamps, MetroPT's duty cycle is not tied to the clock); PRONTO days 2-4, SKAB, HAI 21.03 and the TE runs: auto keeps drift on every one (fit under 2 days or no timestamps), results identical run for run. --method cyclic asked for explicitly: UCI 2/3 (flat profile; the median of 3 removes PS4's one-row blips; section 3's accumulator repair still flags 15/110), MetroPT-3 0/4 (DV_pressure pulses lasting 2+ samples before failures 2 and 3, 217-438 pre-fault rows). Level bands on BattLeDIM 2018 1/14. HELD OUT, BattLeDIM 2019 (A178 mapping), scored once with the frozen default: auto picks cyclic (R2 0.87 on the 15-day normal export) and passes 6/19 (p280, p710 abrupt; p653, p277, p586, p721 incipient), detects 13, 7 runs over 0.5% pre-fault (p514 10, p331 71, p193 129, p680 101, p426 63, p142 9, p123 4 of 576 rows; the tank level T1 among the flagged tags in 5 of the 7); 6 not detected (p523 and p827 abrupt, 4 incipient). Detections are late: 14 h to 5 days after the start (median about 2 days); the first flagged tag is the tank level T1 in 11 of 13. Same runs, drift 0/19 (detects none, no pre-fault flag), level 0/19 (detects 17, all 17 over 0.5% pre-fault)
attempts.runs: 1 held-out pass over 19 runs (deterministic, scored once); 100 development runs per full pass
attempts.why: Kept as an automatic choice: on daily-cycle data it passes runs the drift and level bands cannot (development 8/14, held out 6/19, both 0 with drift), and on every non-cyclic development source auto reproduces the drift method exactly. Limits: the held-out source is the same network as the development one (A178); 5 of the 6 held-out passes rest on flags 1 to 5 days after the start, mostly on the tank level, whose cycle follows the pump rather than the clock, and the same tag causes most pre-fault flags, so a detection here is a flag after the start, not evidence the method saw the leak. Duty cycles not tied to the clock (MetroPT-3) and data already averaged per cycle (UCI) are not detected as cyclic and stay at drift's 1/4 and 0/3. Not tuned further on 2019

attempts.change: Stroke cores plus straight runs: horizontal and vertical runs (0.8% of the long side) opened from the hysteresis ink are added, each cut to pixels at least half as dark as the darkest across the run; then the dip rule: a run pixel less than 0.6 x as dark as the darkest pixel on BOTH sides along the run within 3 stroke widths is not added. attempts.change: line_layers.contract (A177 split): a junction must meet three or more DIFFERENT neighbours. Line that leaves a point and comes back to it, or two lines between the same two places, makes points with three arms but fewer than three neighbours; such a point is passed through (two neighbours) or pruned (one), repeated until every junction left meets three. Error classes found on development: DEXPI C03 (an unkeyed actuator box drawn on the operated valve's stem made three tees; a filled flow arrowhead on the line into the tank made two), DEXPI C01 (one false tee at the plate heat exchanger). contract() is shared, so the same definition applies to every truth built with it (DEXPI, the drawer's routes, the PID2Graph-derived truth) and to dexpi_reader.py

The derived OPEN100 truth changed with it: sheet 1 51 -> 45 true segments and 18 -> 14 junctions (two closed loops in the key graph that touch one symbol each), sheet 5 90 -> 89 and 47 -> 46 (an arrow node with a loop); DEXPI, TE and Bayer truths unchanged. TE revision D and Bayer 1.000 unchanged. Pairwise links identical on all 27 development sheets. examples/from-dexpi-xml/dexpi-c01.* topology unchanged (only the piped_to definition text changed)
